newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: SOCCER-CUBA OPTIMISTIC ON SOCCER FUTURE DESPITE ELIMINATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CUBA OPTIMISTIC ON SOCCER FUTURE DESPITE ELIMINATION.

text.p: Cuba were knocked out of the World Cup qualifying tournament on Sunday but national team coach William Bennett said he was optimistic they could eventually do as well in soccer as they have in other sports.
The Cubans lost 3-0 away to El Salvador, who, along with Canada, progressed from CONCACAF semi-final stage group two to the final six-team stage of the region's qualifying competition.

But, after not even entering in 1986 and 1994, Cuba coach William Bennett said that simply getting to the semi-final stage of the CONCACAF region's competition was an achievement for the cash-strapped Caribbean islanders.
"It would have been very ambitious on our part to want to get to the 1998 finals in France," said Bennett. "What we wanted was to make the first steps, to lay a base for 2000 and after."
He said that his team, which had an average age of 22, had shown potential during the competition in which they eliminated the Cayman Islands and Haiti.
In the semi-final stage itself, Cuba were beaten twice each by Canada and El Salvador but managed an away win against Panama. They elected to play all their "home" matches away for financial reasons.
Cuba has excelled in sports such as athletics, boxing and baseball but soccer has not until now had the same popularity or attention.
The Cubans appeared in the 1938 World Cup finals, when they did not have to play qualifying matches, and beat Romania 2-1 before being hammered 8-0 by Sweden.

El Salvador, who played in the 1970 and 1982 World Cup tournaments, needed only a point to eliminate the Cubans and always looked like getting it after William Renderos scored after just four minutes to the delight of a 25,000 crowd.
Raul Diaz Arce raced between two defenders to score the second in the 32nd minute and Jorge Rodriguez headed in the third early in the second half.
